A · Prompt & presentation ○○ 2026-08-16
Note 02’s last open observation, closed by experiment. Given a task that only asked for a file to be created — no “run it”, no “show me the output” — dsh called write then bash, ran it, and reported the result. Since nothing in the base system prompt instructs verification, the behaviour is a model habit rather than a harness instruction: a harness can be credited with behaviour it never asked for, and telling them apart needs the prompt read and the instruction removed from the task.

Re-ran the Code Mode comparison without the per-file constraint that invalidated the first attempt. Code Mode sent 48.6% less — 214 KB against 417 KB, two run_code calls replacing nine tool calls, final request half the size. C · Context & compaction ○○ 2026-08-16
Tool-result pruning is the first phase of compaction, not a standing policy. Results of 33,189 and 30,348 bytes sat unpruned above the 8,192 threshold because compaction never fired — the pruner is invoked from compaction-basic on context-overflow or pressure, so both mechanisms are gated behind the same event. This note had implied the threshold was a continuous trigger.

C · Context & compaction ○○ 2026-08-16
Code Mode did not flatten the context curve, it moved the cost. The 25 tool schemas left the tools array (26,983 → 908 B) and reappeared in the system prompt (4,063 → 34,998 B); both are re-sent every request, so across the run native sent 843 KB and Code Mode 817 KB — a 3% difference, with one more step. Code Mode is a change of encoding, not a reduction: a capability, not a behaviour.

H · Interop · MCP & ACP ○○ 2026-08-16
Translation is lossy in exactly one direction. A dsh tool exposes over MCP trivially; an imported MCP tool has no domain value to declare, so mcp-client synthesises an output schema describing MCP’s envelope — the canonical value becomes “an MCP response”. And an MCP outputSchema using unsupported vocabulary is silently widened to anything by a swallowed exception, the only silent widening this campaign has found in a specimen that otherwise fails loud.
notes/03-one-tool-two-harnesses.md
D · Tools & permission ○○ 2026-08-16
Phase 3: the same tool built twice. The load-bearing difference is that dsh separates what a tool computed from how the model is told about it — execute returns a canonical value, a pure render projects it — while an MCP tool writes its own sentence inline. Replayable results, Code Mode, and note 02’s structured write wrapper are all one consequence of those two stages existing.
notes/03-one-tool-two-harnesses.md
N · Cross-language embedding ●○ 2026-08-16
A Python client drives a bundled Node runtime over newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdio, and the entire API is eleven operations with one domain verb — session_prompt — plus four serialisable types. The boundary forces three things a shared address space let my toy leave implicit: configuration cannot be defaulted, the harness must be able to call back (a closure becomes a protocol), and observation is literally the session event stream.

L · Provider abstraction ●○ 2026-08-16
There is no single provider seam, there are three separable ones: an adapter registry, a waterfall-interceptable call so a plugin can supply the model per request, and retry as its own plugin on the loop’s error hook — exactly the plugin Thread B predicted from the loop’s empty default resolver. Each scheduled retry is durable before its cancellable wait, so a crash during backoff resumes knowing a retry was owed.
notes/L-provider-abstraction.md
D · Tools & permission ●○ 2026-08-16
Sandbox mode resolves on a three-level ladder: an approved explicit mode outranks the session’s last sandbox/mode event, which outranks the deployment default. So a granted escalation is per-call like every other grant at that seam, and only an explicit mode switch — recorded as a session event and therefore folded on replay — persists.
→ answered G: The escalation ladder is strictly-wider and approval precedes execution. Does a granted escalation persist for the session, or is it one-shot like every other grant at that seam? · notes/G-execution-and-sandboxing.md
G · Execution & sandboxing ○○ 2026-08-16
A sub-agent cannot widen its sandbox: approval policy never means every ask resolves rejected, and a delegated child is pinned to never. But rejected maps to the message “the user rejected tool X” when no user was consulted — so the distinction Thread D praised, between a human refusing and no channel existing, collapses for the one caller least able to find out. The honest unavailable branch exists and this path does not use it.
notes/G-execution-and-sandboxing.md
G · Execution & sandboxing ○○ 2026-08-16
Confinement is real OS-level wrapping — bwrap then Landlock, Seatbelt, Windows restricted tokens — selected by functionally probing candidates rather than detecting the platform, and missing or unusable confinement fails closed rather than returning the original argv. Escalation only ever widens, resolves through approval before anything executes, and shares one implementation across bash and fs so their orderings and error texts cannot drift.

E · Plugin architecture ●○ 2026-08-16
Nothing stops a profile mounting contradictory plugins at runtime because nothing needs to: collisions are startup errors. A duplicate tool name throws, a duplicate subagent provider throws, a second implementation of a cordis service throws, and reserved names like run_code cannot be registered or shadowed. Same shape as restrict() rejecting unknown tools and a depth cap failing at mount — a composition that would be ambiguous does not boot.
→ answered M: Profiles are user-creatable and a profile is an npm-installed plugin set, so mounting a capability is pnpm add. What stops a profile mounting something that contradicts another plugin? · notes/E-plugin-architecture.md

C · Context & compaction ○○ 2026-08-16
Dropping is layered: a model-free size-based pruner keeps head 4096 and tail 1024 of any tool result over 8192 chars with a visible marker, and range compaction selects positionally by retainRatio then substitutes semantically via an LLM summary. Cheap structural pruning first, expensive summarisation only when that is not enough — and nothing is deleted, because a pruned node is shadowed so replay recovers it and the token meter is told what it would have cost.

H · Interop · MCP & ACP ○○ 2026-08-16
Interop is normalization. An MCP server’s tools are registered on ctx.tools under mcp__<server>__<name> and are not a category at all — so without a line of MCP-aware code elsewhere they inherit the three-stage gate, the output.schema and render() contract, per-scope restriction, and Code Mode bindings. Hook dialects and foreign subagent runtimes get the same treatment onto their own seams.

I · Persistence & resumption ○○ 2026-08-16
Five of the session header’s nine fields describe where the session came from rather than what is in it. What must be saved is everything a scope chain would otherwise ask for at runtime, because at resume time there is no parent to ask. Appending is synchronous and validating — a bad event fails at the call site — while durability is write-behind, and a failed background write is reported without rejecting the producer.

K · The host boundary ○○ 2026-08-16
The approval seam takes an answerer, not a human — so an ACP client can hold the permission channel. It fails closed at every level, grants are one-shot with no allow-always outcome, and a decision that cannot be logged is not returned: the audit append and the decision commit together, so no granted permission can exist unwritten. The web UI does nothing structural headless cannot; it composes an answerer.

F · Delegation & sub-agents ○○ 2026-08-16
dsh spawns the real Claude Code Agent SDK and codex app-server as sub-agents. The inheritance guarantees stop at the process boundary — the foreign drivers seed no delegated policy — and the config surface says so: maxDepth accepts provider-managed, and a numeric cap against a provider without a depthLimit capability fails at mount rather than silently.

F · Delegation & sub-agents ○○ 2026-08-16
Delegation is the one recursion budget in a harness with no step cap: maxDepth defaults to 3, 0 forbids it, and depth is monotone because a resumed child counting from zero could delegate as if top-level. A delegated child’s approval policy is pinned to never, so a sub-agent can never ask a human — you cannot widen permissions by delegating.
notes/F-delegation-and-subagents.md
F · Delegation & sub-agents ○○ 2026-08-16
A child joins its parent’s composition by scope-chain link rather than copy, so it inherits tools, prompt sections and plugins live; per-child restriction intersects on top and can only narrow. Policy is the opposite — captured synchronously before the child’s first await, so a parent that loosens its sandbox afterwards does not loosen the child.
